title: Project V — Vulkan Engine
updateNote: Work in progress, updated after every PR.
tagline: A C++20 game engine with a hand-written Vulkan 1.3 renderer.
summary: Built from scratch as the foundation for rendering an Interstellar-style wormhole and skybox.
overview: A C++20 game engine with a hand-written Vulkan 1.3 renderer, built from scratch as the foundation for rendering an Interstellar-style wormhole and skybox.
architecture: Three modules. There's an abstract core interface (IRenderer, IWindow), an engine layer (EnTT ECS, mesh and shader managers, Assimp import), and a Vulkan backend that implements the core interface. Every Vulkan object is a move-only RAII wrapper paired with a fluent, validating builder.
highlights: FBX meshes loaded from disk and uploaded to the GPU
Pipeline cache keyed on shader pairs
Per-object MVP matrices sent as push constants
Frames in flight with fence and semaphore synchronisation
knownIssues: No depth buffer yet, so back faces can draw over front faces (visible in the current render).
Vertex and index buffers are host-visible and not yet staged into device-local memory.
roadmap: Compute pipeline that ray-marches light paths through curved spacetime to render the wormhole's gravitational lensing

title: Project T
tagline: A top-down Windows game built from scratch in C++ and OpenGL.
summary: A top-down game with its own OpenGL renderer and GLSL shaders, with no engine underneath.
overview: A top-down game for Windows built from scratch, with no third-party engine. Rendering, game loop and gameplay are written in C++ with OpenGL and GLSL.
The game runs a timed arena level with collectibles, obstacles and a live frame-time overlay.
highlights: Custom OpenGL renderer with hand-written GLSL shaders
In-game overlay reporting frames per second and milliseconds per frame
Around 119 FPS (8.4 ms per frame) in the arena level

image.alt: Top-down view of a sandy arena with green blocks, red collectibles and a timer reading 182 seconds

title: PBR in OpenGL
tagline: Physically based rendering implemented from scratch.
summary: A physically based rendering implementation written from the ground up in C++ and OpenGL.
overview: Physically based rendering implemented from scratch in C++ and OpenGL, with no rendering library.
The scene shows a textured, reflective sphere above displaced terrain, used to test material response under different lighting.
highlights: PBR shading written by hand in GLSL

image.alt: A reflective blue tiled sphere lit with physically based shading above rough brown terrain

title: Stylized Scene in OpenGL
tagline: A stylized low-poly 3D scene rendered from scratch.
summary: A 3D application that renders a stylized low-poly environment with a custom C++ and OpenGL renderer.
overview: A 3D application built from scratch in C++ and OpenGL to render a stylized low-poly environment: a forest of trees, mountains, a building and terrain under a night sky.
highlights: Hundreds of trees on screen at 120 FPS (8.3 ms per frame)
